subtype: Approach: setting a goal with an amount and date [Thinking]
passage: Note from Vidya, class teacher. Ojas stayed after maths with a folded paper. He wants a secondhand bicycle that costs 4,000 rupees and has given himself six months. “That's a lot,” he said, and I stayed quiet. He counted aloud: “Six months is about twenty-six weeks. 4,000 divided by 26 is about 155 a week. My allowance is 200 a week. So I'd still have 45 for snacks.” He laughed, surprised. “It's not as big as it sounded.” He wrote the target date at the top of the page and the weekly figure beside it. I asked only whether he would tell his parents, and he said tonight. I will ask him about it in a month.

qa.q: How much does the secondhand bicycle cost?
What was Ojas feeling when he finished counting?
qa.a: Ojas felt surprised and encouraged, since he laughed and said it was not as big as it sounded.

qa.q: What could Ojas do if a week's saving falls short?
qa.a: He could move the date a little or earn small extra money, since a fixed weekly figure with some slack keeps the goal alive.

qa.q: How might Ojas's parents feel when he tells them the plan tonight?
qa.a: They may feel pleased and proud that Ojas worked out the numbers himself, and more willing to back the goal.

grounding: A teen turns a bicycle price and a six-month deadline into a weekly saving figure and finds it more realistic than he thought.

subtype: Approach: setting a goal with an amount and date [Thinking]
passage:
Sunday
Found the bicycle I want: a secondhand geared one at the repair shop near the market, 4,000 rupees. Babu Uncle at the shop says he can keep it aside for a while if I pay a little first.
First reaction: impossible. My allowance is 250 a week, and 4,000 sounds like a mountain.
But then I did the maths properly on the back of my notebook. Six months is about 26 weeks. 4,000 divided by 26 is roughly 154. Call it 160 a week, to be safe. That leaves 90 a week for everything else.
Ninety is tight but not terrible: no more samosas every day, maybe twice a week. Himani said I can come to her place for cricket instead of the gaming parlour.
So it's not a mountain. It's 160 rupees, 26 times.
Starting this Monday. Target: 12 October.
– Yusuf

qa.q: How much does Yusuf plan to save each week?
How did Yusuf feel before and after doing the maths?
qa.a: Yusuf felt it was impossible, like a mountain, then relieved and hopeful once it became 160 rupees a week.

qa.q: What else could Yusuf do if 90 a week feels too tight?
qa.a: Talk it over with a parent, and perhaps move the target date a little later so the weekly amount is gentler.

qa.q: How might Himani see the new plan?
qa.a: Himani seems supportive, offering cricket at home as a free alternative to the gaming parlour.

grounding: Shows a teen turning a 4,000-rupee bicycle goal over six months into a weekly saving figure and finding it more realistic than feared.

passage:
Francis: found a used cycle for 4000. i'll never afford that
Maria: how long do you have?
Francis: want it by the summer holidays. like 6 months
Maria: ok so divide it
Francis: by what
Maria: weeks. 6 months is about 26 weeks
Francis: 4000/26... 154?
Maria: yes. round it to 160
Francis: i get 300 a week from mum
Maria: so you'd still have 140 left for everything else
Francis: huh. that's actually doable
Maria: told you. write 160 on a sticky note and put it on your mirror
Francis: and not buy chips every day
Maria: and not buy chips every day 😄
Francis: ok. starting monday. 26 mondays

qa.q: How much does Francis get each week from mum?
How did Francis feel at the start of the chat, and at the end?
qa.a: Francis felt hopeless at first, sure he could never afford it, then surprised and hopeful when the weekly figure turned out doable.

qa.q: What else could make the plan easier to keep?
qa.a: Telling mum about the goal, so she knows the plan and can suggest a safe place to keep the savings.

qa.q: How does Maria see Francis's worry?
qa.a: Maria sees a maths problem rather than a hopeless one, and patiently walks him through it with a bit of teasing.

grounding: Shows a teen dividing a 4,000-rupee cycle goal over six months into a weekly amount and finding it more realistic than he thought.
